correctness.rationale: The 12-vertex LCF-defined cubic graph has exactly 4096 vertex subsets. Two cycle tests and direct maximum-degree checks establish all four face lists. Four explicit deterministic acyclic matchings are exhaustively topologically sorted over 456, 3244, 11833 and 13206 covering relations, yielding critical-cell counts (one vertex plus 3 degree-2 cells), (one vertex plus 1 degree-3 cell), (one vertex plus 4 degree-6 and 1 degree-7), and (one vertex plus 4 degree-6 and 2 degree-7). Signed integer Morse elimination, independently checked as an integral chain map on every simplex, gives zero d=2 boundary and d=3 boundary with exactly one +1 entry. Hurewicz in dimension 6 and a primitive seven-to-six cancellation prove the four integral homotopy types. Explicit cycle lifting yields source-basis vectors and target images; the H6 inclusion is a split rank-2 map Z^4 to Z^3 and H7 an isomorphism, proving the integral interval decomposition. An unrelated exact simplicial F2 boundary-rank computation confirms the Betti groups. This is finite exhaustive mathematics for one graph, with no unproved infinite extrapolation.

value.rationale: The Frucht graph is the canonical smallest-order asymmetric cubic graph, while induced-forest complexes encode feasible complements of feedback-vertex sets. The full four-stage filtration is naturally forced by its maximum degree three and gives a meaningful exact topology-and-persistence question, not an arbitrary parameter slice. In degree six the terminal stage kills two existing classes yet creates a new class, a structural phenomenon invisible from the individual ranks and requiring explicit integral map computations. The split integer barcode and mixed-dimensional homotopy types are reusable finite benchmarks for forest filtrations; the previously known d=0 stage is context, not the claimed gain.
